editorial.headline: Safety Glass Manufacturing With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 23112 covers the manufacture of tempered, laminated, insulating and other safety glass, open nationally to PMA and not blocked in Bali under the stated risk reading.
editorial.body:
KBLI 23112 is the manufacturing home for safety glass: glass made to perform beyond ordinary sheet glass in strength, protection, layering, insulation or a comparable safety function. The record names tempered safety glass, laminated safety glass, insulating safety glass and other safety glass within the same activity. In plain terms, this is not a trading or installation category; it is about making the glass product itself, where the defining feature is that the finished material is engineered as safety glass.

The registration profile is broad. The activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, so the same KBLI can describe a small producer as well as a large industrial operation, provided the registered activity remains the manufacture of safety glass. Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward: the code is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. For founders reading the code from a foreign-investment angle, that means the national record does not impose a reduced foreign-share cap for this activity.

The Bali reading is equally important because it does not simply mirror the national headline. Bali’s moratorium rule, as stated in the record, blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI across the province on a permanent, island-wide basis. That is the gate a founder has to test before treating a nationally open activity as available in Bali. Here, the record says the activity is not blocked: at Besar scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which places it outside the blocked Low and Medium-Low band described by the moratorium.

So the honest picture is open nationally and not blocked in Bali on the record provided. That does not turn the category into a casual checkbox; it simply means the Bali-side moratorium is not the barrier identified for this KBLI. The decisive facts are narrow and concrete: this is safety-glass manufacturing, it is open to every listed scale, it is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and Bali’s listed status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK because the stated risk position keeps it outside the moratorium block.
